method.monotone_test: count of rising steps in the normalised profile
method.normalisation: each profile divided by its own value at the inner edge
method.two_maxima_reported_separately: The matter density and the mass gradient can leave the boundary at different radii. Merging them would overstate what is resolved: at the deepest edge the matter maximum stands 22% above the boundary value while the mass gradient is flat to 0.6% across the same two nodes.
method.why_normalise: The amplitude is known to grow with edge depth. Normalising asks the separate question of whether the shape also moves, which an amplitude alone cannot answer.

scope_note: A construction check on finite marched collars. It does not measure the actual universe. A gradient zone in one numerical construction is not evidence that any real object has one.
what_this_measures: The shape of the compressed layer, which the mass-shell reduction measured only as an amplitude. At the compression peak, whether the density falls monotonically from the inner edge with no interface, and whether the half-width of that falloff narrows as the boundary deepens.
